messages.subject: Re: Interaction terms for a two factor and two level experimental design
messages.subject_clean: Interaction terms for a two factor and two level experimental design
messages.body_plain:
Hi Priya,

How many biological replicates in your data? If only 4 biological replicates (the design is time-course), then your annotation file is correct. But if 16 biological replicates (the design is group comparison), then the BioReplicate column should have 16 unique IDs.

For the second question, the degrees of freedom are estimated from the linear model and thus are the same for all the comparisons. The degrees of freedom is 9 because MSstats thinks the data has a time-course design.

For the third question, MSstats doesn't output such a trellis display. But you can use ggplot2 package to easily make the figure based on the input data to dataProcess() function. Here are some ggplot2 examples for such figures: https://plotly.com/ggplot2/facet_wrap/.

Best,
Ting

Hi,

I would like to add one comment. I guess your design is group comparison because there are female and male groups and infected and uninfected groups, which might not overlap each other.
Based on the annotation you shared, MSstats recognizes that one subject (BioReplicate=1) has 'female', 'male', 'infected', and 'uninfected' samples, which might not be your design.
If you have 4 infected female + 4 uninfected female + 4 infected male + 4 uninfected male = total 16 people (ex. 4 infected female are different from 4 uninfected female), it should has 16 unique IDs, as Ting said.

Best,
- Meena

this should be the order of group in contrast matrix. For example, in the matrix, c(a,b,c,d), 'a' should be the constant for FI, 'b' should be the constant for FUI, 'c' should be the constant for MI, 'd' should be the constant for MUI. Therefore, the contrast matrix should be updated.

#I compared Male uninfected to male infected : MUI-MI
comparison1<-matrix(c(0, 0, -1, 1),nrow=1)
# Comparison of female uninfected to female infected : FUI-MI
comparison2<-matrix(c(-1, 1, 0, 0),nrow=1)
#comparison of male uninfected to female uninfected : MUI-FUI
comparison3<-matrix(c(0, -1,0,1),nrow=1)
#comparison of male infected to female infected : MI-FI
comparison4<-matrix(c(-1, 0, 1, 0),nrow=1)

#contrast for testing interaction between sex and infection

comparison5 <- matrix(c(1,-1,-1,1), nrow=1)

Interaction seems correct.

HTH
- Meena

My mistake was to take the wrong quantitation column which resulted in this weird outlier problem.

DIA NN however seems to report the same number of ions for every precursor even if the quant for one transition is empty
7

basically:
DIA NN output
Exp     Pep    Frag.Quant
Run1  pep1  10,15
Run2  pep1  20,30

becomes
Exp     Pep    y5  y6
Run1  pep1  10  15
Run2  pep1  20  30

I will post how the analysis will go if anybody else wants to use DIA NN and msstats.

Best, Klemens

messages.subject: Re: big dataset
messages.subject_clean: big dataset
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

the dataProcess function does several things and at each step there's something you can do to improve the running time. I'll assume there's no fractionation in your data (if there is, only some details change):

 - dataProcess requires that there is a row for each feature in each run. If your input data satisfy this requirement, there will be no need for potentially lengthy computations,

- then, dataProcess performs normalization. If you can normalize data in an efficient way outside of dataProcess, it should speed it up significantly (just set normalization = "NONE"),

- selecting features for summarization via "highQuality" method can take some time - if you want speed, choose "topN" with a low N (3 is the default for this method, but by default dataProcess uses all features),

- another operation is finding values that will be considered as censored. You can set maxQuantileforCensored = NULL to skip this (and perhaps do it outside of dataProcess function),

- with data in the right format (normalized, with a row for every run and feature etc), you can run dataProcess for each protein separately or for batches of proteins and parallelize your code.

Btw we will be releasing a new version of MSstats in October. The new version will be easier to work with for big datasets

Kind regards,
Mateusz Staniak

> - then, dataProcess performs normalization. If you can normalize data in an efficient way outside of dataProcess, it should speed it up significantly (just set normalization = "NONE"),
>
> - selecting features for summarization via "highQuality" method can take some time - if you want speed, choose "topN" with a low N (3 is the default for this method, but by default dataProcess uses all features),
>
> - another operation is finding values that will be considered as censored. You can set maxQuantileforCensored = NULL to skip this (and perhaps do it outside of dataProcess function),
>
> - with data in the right format (normalized, with a row for every run and feature etc), you can run dataProcess for each protein separately or for batches of proteins and parallelize your code.
>
>
> Btw we will be releasing a new version of MSstats in October. The new version will be easier to work with for big datasets
>
>
> Kind regards,
> Mateusz Staniak

messages.subject_clean: big dataset
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

datatProcess creates three columns from data in the standard 10-column format:
- peptide = PeptideSequence + PrecursorCharge
- transition = FragmentIon + ProductCharge
- feature = peptide + transition

If your features are the same as peptide, FragmentIon and ProductCharge columns should have a single value (can be NA - that's how converter functions XtoMSstatsFormat fill these columns in).
With features defined this way, dataProcess make sure that each feature has a row for each run by filling in Intensity=NA if the row was missing.

The new version of the package is in development on Github at Vitek-Lab/MSstatsConvert and Vitek-Lab/MSstats-dev but the changes are not documented properly, yet, and it's still under heavy testing, unfortunately.

Kind regards,
Mateusz

messages.subject_clean: multi kit, multi fraction PD experiment error
messages.body_plain:
This error is because of missing rows in the annotation file. It seems like some channel information is missing in some runs. For example, channel 129N is missing from 078_0004_01C_R_Kit3Fraction5_13AUG20_PLA_HUM_ECL_0012_PA_135MIN_MNM_RS_01.raw (see the following scrrenshot)

Another example, channel 131C is missing from 078_0004_01C_R_Kit2Fraction32_13AUG20_PLA_HUM_ECL_0012_PA_135MIN_MNM_RS_01.raw.

MSstatsTMT requries info for each run and each channel. If the channle is empty sample, you can put "Empty" under Condition and Bioreplicate columns. You can use the following code to check which runs have issue:

library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
MSstatsTMT_annotDB %>% group_by(Run) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(Channel)) %>%
  filter(n < 11)
